sections.title: Pros
sections.narration: The upsides first: plain white rice is easy on many stomachs. Its lower fibre and blandness make it a practical recovery or tolerance food for some people, which is more specific than generic convenience. Cheap and easy to scale as a staple. White rice earns real-world value from being affordable, shelf-stable, and easy to cook in large batches. Neutral enough to pair with almost anything. That flexibility helps explain why it stays common even when its standalone nutrition case is weak.

sections.title: Cons
sections.narration: Cons next: refining strips out much of the fibre and micronutrient value. That is the central reason white rice scores worse than intact whole grains. It is mostly starch with limited standalone nutrition. The protein, fibre, and micronutrient payload are all modest for the calories. Carb quality changes a lot with rice type and preparation. That makes the exact glycemic story hard to lock honestly from a single dry-rice record.
